content.text: Single continuous cinematic camera move, no cuts. Stylised painterly 3D illustration with the graphic language of a hand-painted game world - bold silhouettes, simplified sculpted forms, soft painterly surfaces without fine photoreal texture detail, and strong contrast between deep shadow and glowing accent light. Never photorealistic and never live-action, but equally never comic or cartoon. Deep violet and midnight-blue base throughout, structures and light in royal and electric violet. Warm orange reserved for sunset light, backlight, rim light and highlights - present but never dominant. This violet-and-orange palette is present in every single frame including the very last one; the image never desaturates into grey, neutral blue or realistic daylight colour. Soft bloom, volumetric haze, shallow depth of field, subtle film grain, calm slightly surreal atmosphere. Organic surfaces meet digital light structures. No neon cyberpunk city, no text, no letters, no logos, no signage. The dragonfly flies over the flowering meadow toward the dark glass facade of the modern office building, seen from behind. She is a precision-engineered machine of dark chrome and anodised violet, with large faceted eyes and two pairs of long transparent wings veined with glowing violet nodes, edges catching warm orange rim light - elegant, constructed, never cute or cartoonish. Her wings beat visibly and continuously as she flies, sweeping in fast soft-blurred strokes; they are never held still and never frozen open in one fixed position. Her luminous violet trail is continuous and always visible: it streams behind her whenever she flies, in open air just as much as near a surface, and never switches off. She reaches the building and rises along the facade, tracing its lines closely. The low sun keeps the position it has in the opening frame: low on the horizon to the right, behind the building. It never moves or jumps sides; the warm orange light comes from the right and from behind throughout, and the left flank of the facade stays in deep violet shadow. The building is completely dark and dormant. Light appears only in her wake and never ahead of her: as her trail passes over glass and concrete, violet nodes ignite at the corners of the existing window frames, light lines run along the floor edges, columns and seams of the facade, and behind the glass the floors she has already passed wake and glow warmly from within. The architecture is already there and is never rebuilt; no new windows, panels or shapes ever appear. The only thing that ever appears is the violet light network laying itself over the structure that already exists. The light she leaves behind is permanent: once ignited, nodes, lines and lit floors stay fully bright for the rest of the shot and never fade, dim or go dark. The facade she has passed stays lit behind her while the facade ahead of her stays dark. She rises to a single window standing tilted open in the now glowing facade - hinged along its bottom edge and leaning inward at the top, leaving a dark wedge-shaped gap along its upper edge - and slows to hover in front of it, her wings still beating. The camera keeps enough distance for the whole tilted window and the lit facade around it to stay clearly visible, and never closes in to a tight close-up of the dragonfly. The camera follows the dragonfly, which leads the shot and stays visible throughout. The camera never pulls back and never loses the dragonfly. The shot ends with the dragonfly clearly in frame ahead of the camera, seen from behind, hovering in front of the tilted-open window, her violet trail still streaming behind her, the dark wedge-shaped gap above the tilted pane clearly readable as the way in.
